title: India Seeks US Action After Illinois Temple Plot as Police Reveal New Details
excerpt: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called for zero tolerance for hate-motivated violence, as Aurora police detailed the accused’s 13 minutes in the temple lot and said the rifle-jam account remains unconfirmed.
body:
• India's MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India is deeply concerned by the alleged Aurora temple plot and its reported anti-Hindu, racist nature, and has taken note of the US arrest and charges.
  • Aurora police said Thursday the accused's red Acura RDX was in the temple parking lot for about 13 minutes on Sunday, that he appears to have acted alone — and that police have not confirmed his rifle actually jammed.
  • Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi, whose family has worshipped at the temple for some 40 years, will seek a hate-crime investigation and federal security grants for houses of worship.
  • Charges include a Class X felony terrorist threat and a Class 3 felony over a short-barrel rifle; the next hearing is October 30 in Rolling Meadows, with federal charges still under review.

India has responded formally to the alleged plot to attack a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois. MEA Official Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, responding to media queries, said India is deeply concerned by the alleged plot and its reported anti-Hindu, racist nature, including references to violence against people of Indian origin, Livemint reported. India has taken note of the US law-enforcement action — the arrest, detention and charges — and Jaiswal called for greater vigilance, zero tolerance for hate-motivated violence, and decisive action to protect the Indian community, along with a thorough investigation and measures to prevent a recurrence.

The statement lands on top of the case we reported yesterday, when 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis was charged over the alleged plot. That report covered his alleged eight-page manifesto and his claim that his rifle jammed. Thursday's police briefing added new facts — and one important caveat.

What Police Said Thursday

Aurora police told a press conference, reported by FOX 32 Chicago, that surveillance shows Paporakis's red Acura RDX entering the temple parking lot at about 12:25 p.m. on Sunday and leaving at about 12:38 p.m.; he was alone, and was back in Palatine shortly before 2 p.m. Investigators believe he acted alone. His seized devices are being examined at the FBI's Chicago Regional Computer Forensic Laboratory.

Police also drew a line under one detail: they have not confirmed that his gun jammed, and have not determined where a video of a rifle failing to fire was recorded or where the alleged shooting attempt occurred. The jam account comes from what Paporakis allegedly told a co-worker — that his rifle failed after he tried to shoot at a man from his vehicle. Prosecutors say that on October 10 he told the same co-worker he could not wait to kill Indian people, according to Livemint.

A Congressman Whose Family Worships There

US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi said his family has worshipped at the Aurora temple for about 40 years and his parents were there all day Sunday; he learned of the alleged attack only when police announced it late Wednesday. He plans to ask for a hate-crime investigation and called for federal security grants for houses of worship.

Charges and What Happens Next

The charges, per Livemint, are a terrorist threat — a Class X felony in Illinois — and a Class 3 felony for possessing a rifle with a barrel shorter than 16 inches. Federal charges are still being determined, with the FBI's Chicago office and federal and local prosecutors reviewing the case. Paporakis's next court appearance is October 30 in Rolling Meadows.

For the congregation, the immediate question is practical: Diwali is days away, the temple will be full, and its most prominent worshipper is now asking Washington for security money. Delhi, for its part, has put its concern on the record — the next move belongs to the US investigation.
image_caption: The entrance of a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois, flanked by a white elephant statue. India said it is in touch with US authorities after an alleged plot to attack a temple in the state.
nri_angle: New Delhi’s public response, days before Diwali, puts temple security and anti-India hate in the US at the centre of a diplomatic conversation.
author: Diaspora Desk
